evidence: Injected nine corruption and absence classes against a committed artifact (python3 -I corruption_injector.py, exit 0, all nine PASS) and ran 11 unittest cases (python3 -I -m unittest discover, 11 tests OK). A wrong hash, a byte count one higher than the committed bytes, bytes truncated after hashing, an absent path, a nonexistent commit, a tree locator instead of a blob and a file:// locator were each refused at ingestion and classified RECOVERY_REQUIRED with an explicit read-back mismatch, read-back failure or non-durable error; in every refusing class the immutable capsule stayed intact and hash-matched, and a rerun committed from that capsule reached PARENT_INGESTED with zero errors. A zero-byte artifact was refused by the seeded contract with '$.artifacts[0].bytes: must be an integer >= 1' and an artifact-free committed result with '$.artifacts: committed result requires at least one artifact'. Overwriting the worktree file with different bytes after the commit changed nothing: ingestion read the committed object and still reached PARENT_INGESTED, which is the property that makes hash coverage meaningful. read_object_bytes also raised ValueError for http:// and for a bare relative path. false_completions_observed was 0 and verify_chain stayed clean through refusal and rerun.
falsifiable_hypothesis: A corrupt or missing artifact is refused at ingestion and routed to recovery rather than accepted.
limitations: Corruption is injected at the claim and locator level plus a real truncated re-commit; the git object store itself was not corrupted, because a content-addressed object cannot be silently altered in place, so that direction is untestable rather than untested.

The ingestion guard for an artifact-free result is unreachable for a committed result because the seeded contract rejects that document first; the refusal is equivalent but comes from a different layer than the code suggests.
A refused result is still persisted to control/tasks/<task>/result-<hash>.json, which is what makes the refusal auditable but also means corrupt callback bytes accumulate in the control plane.
provider_run_id is NOT_SUPPORTED because this runtime exposes no subagent spawn tool and therefore no separate provider run identifier.
